description: Keeps the git pins in apm.yml current for agent packages from webgrip's Forgejo.

Renovate's built-in apm manager only reads the string form (host/owner/repo#ref), and on a non-GitHub host APM itself only splits a subdirectory off that form at prompts/, instructions/ or collections/. webgrip pins packages and skills by subdirectory (packages/<name>, skills/<name>) in the object form (git, path, ref), so these regex managers read that form instead.

Every bump of an agent package runs `agentstd install` as a post-upgrade task, so apm.lock.yaml and every file APM writes arrive in the same pull request: a bump of webgrip/agent-standards runs the CLI from its new tag, any other package from the agent-standards release this preset names, which Renovate keeps current in this repository. The self-hosted config must allow the two commands (homelab-cluster configmap-forgejo.yaml).

The branches these bumps land in come from parts/agent-package-group.json, which every gate applies after the first-party part: Renovate takes a branch's post-upgrade task from the first update in it, sorted by name, so an agent package needs a branch of its own for the install to run with the right tag. This overlay itself decides no grouping, so its place in extends does not matter.

customManagers.description: A skill from webgrip/ai-skills, pinned by its per-skill tag <skill>-vX.Y.Z.
A package from another webgrip repository, such as agent-standards, pinned by a vX.Y.Z tag.
The agentstd CLI pinned to an agent-standards tag in mise.toml tasks, so the tool moves with the packages.

packageRules.description: Every pin of an agent package installs with agentstd, so the lockfile and the generated agent files arrive in the bump's pull request. A bump of agent files changes what agents read, not what the repository ships, so it lands as chore(agents) and cuts no release.
A bump of agent-standards installs with the CLI from the tag it bumps to, so the lockfile and the generated agent files match that release.
